issues.legal_issue: A murder conviction may be sustained on reliable, corroborated eyewitness evidence despite factional enmity and the acquittal of co-accused when the evidence against the convicted person has distinguishing incriminating features.
material_facts: The prosecution witnesses were acknowledged to be inimical toward the accused group, so their evidence required careful scrutiny.
The witnesses identified the appellant as the person who fired the fatal shot in broad daylight.
Medical evidence corroborated the eyewitness account and the first information report named the appellant as the shooter.
The co-accused were acquitted because their alleged participation was doubtful, including because no spear injuries were found; the evidence against the appellant was distinguishable.
The High Court had assessed the evidence and upheld the appellant’s conviction.
issues.conclusion: The appellant’s murder conviction was rightly upheld; the acquittal of the co-accused did not require his acquittal.
issues.legal_principle: In an appeal by special leave under Article 136, the Court ordinarily accepts the High Court’s appraisal of eyewitness evidence unless there is a failure of justice, a material misreading or disregard of evidence, a substantial error of law or procedure, or an important question of principle. Where factional enmity may lead witnesses to implicate innocent members of the opposing group, the evidence must be sifted carefully and only those against whom it is safe to rely on the evidence may be convicted. An acquittal of co-accused does not by itself require acquittal of another accused unless the cases are completely identical and lack additional incriminating features. No earlier case is cited for these principles.

rule.if: murder_conviction_appeal and factional_witnesses and appellant_identified_by_eyewitnesses and appellant_evidence_corrobated and co_accused_acquitted_on_distinct_doubt

predicates.murder_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a conviction for murder.
predicates.factional_witnesses: The prosecution witnesses belong to a faction inimical to the accused and their evidence therefore calls for careful scrutiny.
predicates.appellant_identified_by_eyewitnesses: Eyewitnesses identify the appellant as the person who committed the fatal act.
predicates.appellant_evidence_corrobated: Evidence independent of the eyewitness account corroborates the case against the appellant.
predicates.co_accused_acquitted_on_distinct_doubt: Co-accused are acquitted because their alleged participation is doubtful, while the evidence against the appellant has distinguishing incriminating features.

issues.definition: When a murder conviction appeal involves inimical witnesses but the appellant is identified by eyewitnesses, the case against the appellant is corroborated, and acquittals of co-accused rest on distinct doubts, the appellant’s conviction is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: The prosecution need not call every person said to have witnessed an offence if it produces the material witnesses and has not deliberately withheld a material witness.
material_facts: The appellant argued that some people named as witnesses in the first information report had not been examined.
The Court found that the appellant had not shown how their absence made the prosecution case less trustworthy or that any material and important witness had been deliberately withheld.
The prosecution had produced witnesses considered necessary to unfold its case.
issues.conclusion: The non-examination of the additional persons did not undermine the prosecution case.
issues.legal_principle: The prosecution is not bound to produce every person said to have witnessed the occurrence. It need produce the material witnesses necessary to unfold its case, without unnecessary or redundant multiplication of witnesses. No earlier case or statutory provision is cited for this proposition.

rule.if: criminal_trial and some_alleged_witnesses_not_called and material_witnesses_produced and no_material_witness_deliberately_withheld and no_demonstrated_prejudice

predicates.criminal_trial: The proceeding is a criminal trial in which the prosecution must prove its case.
predicates.some_alleged_witnesses_not_called: Some people said to have witnessed the occurrence are not called by the prosecution.
predicates.material_witnesses_produced: The prosecution calls the witnesses it considers necessary to present the material account of the offence.
predicates.no_material_witness_deliberately_withhel: The evidence does not show that the prosecution deliberately kept back an important witness.
predicates.no_demonstrated_prejudice: The absence of the uncalled witnesses is not shown to make the prosecution case less trustworthy.

issues.definition: When a criminal prosecution omits some alleged witnesses but produces its material witnesses without deliberate withholding or demonstrated prejudice, the omission does not undermine the prosecution case.

issues.legal_issue: An allegation of absconding is a weak circumstance, and a conviction may stand without relying on it when the accused was not given an opportunity to explain it and the remaining evidence independently establishes guilt.
material_facts: The High Court had taken the appellant’s alleged absconding into account.
The circumstance of absconding was not put to the appellant during his examination, so he could not offer an explanation.
The Court found that the eyewitness and corroborating evidence established guilt beyond reasonable doubt even without considering absconding.
issues.conclusion: The conviction was sustainable without relying on the alleged absconding, which had not been put to the appellant for explanation.
issues.legal_principle: Absconding, even if proved, is normally a somewhat weak link in a chain of circumstances. It may fortify a conclusion already supported by trustworthy eyewitness evidence, but an innocent person may also keep out of the way after learning of a false implication. No earlier case or statutory provision is cited for this proposition.

predicates.criminal_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.alleged_absconding_not_put_for_explanati: The alleged absconding is not put to the accused so that the accused can explain it.
predicates.independent_reliable_evidence_establishe: Evidence apart from the alleged absconding reliably establishes guilt.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a criminal conviction, alleged absconding was not put to the accused for explanation, and other reliable evidence establishes guilt, the conviction is sustainable without relying on absconding.

issues.legal_issue: A death sentence may be reduced to imprisonment for life when the circumstances of the case make that lesser sentence sufficient to meet the ends of justice.
material_facts: The trial court imposed a death sentence for murder, and the High Court confirmed it.
The Court held that the discretion between death and imprisonment for life had been widened by the amendment to Section 367(5) of the Code of Criminal Procedure made by Act 26 of 1955.
Considering the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, the Court concluded that imprisonment for life would meet the ends of justice.
issues.conclusion: The death sentence was reduced to imprisonment for life.
issues.legal_principle: After the 1955 amendment to Section 367(5) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the court’s discretion in choosing between death and imprisonment for life was wider. The Court applied that discretion in light of the particular circumstances and held that imprisonment for life would meet the ends of justice. No earlier case is cited for this sentencing decision.

predicates.murder_sentencing_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the sentence for murder.
predicates.death_sentence_imposed: A death sentence has been imposed for the offence.
predicates.case_circumstances_make_life_sentence_su: The circumstances of the case make imprisonment for life sufficient to meet the ends of justice.

issues.definition: When a murder sentencing appeal challenges an imposed death sentence and the circumstances make imprisonment for life sufficient, the death sentence is reduced to imprisonment for life.
